stem: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application currently keeps one value in its source code. The value is an application endpoint URL that the team updates by hand a few times each year. The company wants to move the value out of the code and read it at run time through the AWS SDK. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?
keywords: an application endpoint URL that the team updates by hand a few times each year

options.text: Store the value as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager with the AWS managed key aws/secretsmanager, and turn on automatic rotation.
options.why: It works, but Secrets Manager is [billed per secret per month](../facts/parameter-store.md#parameter-store-vs-secrets-manager-cost-row), and a URL that people change by hand needs no rotation.

options.text: Store the value as a standard String parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, and change the parameter value when required.
options.why: Parameter Store is [a centralized configuration data store](../facts/parameter-store.md#parameter-store-what-it-is), and the AWS comparison table lists its [standard tier free](../facts/parameter-store.md#parameter-store-vs-secrets-manager-cost-row).

options.text: Store the value as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager, encrypt it with a new customer managed KMS key, and turn on automatic rotation.
options.why: It works, but it adds the charge for each secret and a customer managed key at [$1/month](../facts/kms.md#kms-price-key-storage-per-month) for a value that needs no rotation.

options.text: Store the value as an advanced SecureString parameter in Parameter Store, and attach a NoChangeNotification policy to the parameter.
options.why: It works, but an advanced parameter costs [$0.05 per advanced parameter per month](../facts/parameter-store.md#parameter-store-price-advanced-parameter), and the stem asks for no notification.
options.misconception: Production configuration needs the advanced tier of Parameter Store.

explanation: The value is plain configuration that people change by hand, so it needs no rotation and no notification. In the AWS comparison table, Parameter Store has its [standard tier free](../facts/parameter-store.md#parameter-store-vs-secrets-manager-cost-row), while Secrets Manager is [billed per secret per month](../facts/parameter-store.md#parameter-store-vs-secrets-manager-cost-row). The advanced tier and a customer managed key each add a charge that buys nothing here. The cheapest store that meets the need is a standard String parameter.
takeaway: Plain configuration that people change by hand goes into a standard parameter, which has no additional charge.
twin: If the stem said "a database password that company policy requires to be rotated automatically every 30 days" instead: Secrets Manager, because credential rotation in Parameter Store is [None](../facts/parameter-store.md#parameter-store-vs-secrets-manager-rotation-row).
